newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian parliament rejects budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Russian parliament rejects budget cuts.

text.p: Russia's opposition-dominated parliament threw out government plans to slash spending on Monday but ministers vowed to press on regardless once the State Duma starts its summer holidays this week.

Deputies in the communist-led lower chamber voted by 210 votes to 112 to reject at the first reading a government bill that would have slashed spending under the 1997 budget by 108 trillion roubles ($18.8 billion) or about a fifth of the total.
The State Duma also rejected by 195 to 137 votes a plan put forward by a communist deputy that would have cut spending by just 39 trillion roubles.
Monday's votes are the latest moves in a long tussle between the reform-minded government and the Duma over economic policy.

The government bill, which was receiving its first reading after weeks of stalling by the communist-led lower house, was prompted by a massive shortfall of more than 40 percent in tax revenue in the first three months of this year.

Reformist ministers had offered to reduce the amount of the cuts, known as sequestration, to about 88 trillion roubles and to seek new sources of revenue. But after failing to agree a compromise, decided to put the original bill to the Duma.

The government has said that, with or without the support of the Duma, which rises for the summer recess on Tuesday, cuts in spending will take place because the state is simply unable to pay its bills.

Deputy Finance Minister Vladimir Petrov told reporters after the vote that the government would hold talks with the Duma parties on Monday and Tuesday but would, in the absence of an accord, press on alone with bringing order to public finances.
